BAGONG PLIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City HON. ANTONIO JOSE A. BARCELON Mayor Office of the Mayor Nasugbu, Batangas Dear Hon. Barcelon: s. This has reference to your letter dated 28 December 2023 requesting for clarification on the "interruption" of your term of office as Municipal Mayor and your eligibility to run for Municipal Mayor of Nasugbu, Batangas in 2025 The facts are stated as follows: You have been serving as Mayor of Nasugbu, Batangas since 2016 and the present term will end in 2025. You were dismissed from service by the Office of the Ombudsman on 5 March 2018 but was later reversed in a Resolution dated 7 March 2019. On 28 July 2023, a suspension order from the Ombudsman was meted against you due to negligence committed by the BAC members. Despite a Motion for Reconsideration, no action has since been taken on the matter by the aforementioned office. Consequently, this Department implemented the 90-day suspension. These facts led you to herein request for clarification on whether the two instances mentioned are considered interruption of your term of office for purposes of running again as Municipal Mayor in 2025. We opine. Jurisprudence has laid down the circumstances which would define an effective interruption, to wit: From all the above, we conclude that the "interruption" of a term exempting an elective official from the three-term limit rule is one that involves no less than the involuntary loss of title to office. The elective official must have involuntarily left his office for a length of time, however short, for an effective interruption to occur. This has to be the case if the thrust of Section 8, Article X and its [strict] intent are to be faithfully served, i.e., to limit an elective official's continuous stay in office to no more than three consecutive terms, using "voluntary renunciation" as an example and standard of what does not constitute an interruption. Thus, based on this standard, loss of office by operation of law, being involuntary, is an effective interruption of service within a term, as we held in Montebon. On the other hand, temporary inability or disqualification to exercise the functions of an elective post, even if involuntary, should not be considered an effective interruption of a term "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

because it does not involve the loss of title to office or at least an effective break from holding office; the office holder, while retaining title, is simply barred from exercising the function[s] of his office for a reason provided by law. An interruption occurs when the term is broken because the office holder lost the right to hold on to his office, and cannot be equated with the failure to render service. The latter occurs during an office holder's term when he retains title to the office but cannot exercise his functions for reasons established by law. Of course, the [term] "failure to serve" cannot be used once the right to office is lost; without the right to hold office or to serve, then no service can be rendered so that none is really Iostl. Furthermore, jurisprudence provides that an Ombudsman's dismissal order is immediately executory and, once executed, the public officer ceases to have title for the time being. Hence, it should be considered as an interruption of his term2. Succinctly put, in Aldovino Jr. vs. Comelec, suspension from office is not an effective interruption for purposes of applying the three-term limit rule. On the other hand, Tallado vs. Comelec, provided that dismissal from services regardless of length and after effectively serving is considered an interruption for purposes of applying the three- term limit rule under the Constitution and the Local Government Code. Applying the foregoing to the instant case, we opine that considering your dismissal was not implemented, the doctrine under the Tallado case cannot be invoked. As to the remedial measures availed of such as a Motion for Reconsideration, the same shall not affect the decision of the Ombudsman from being executory. Thus, the mere fact of being placed under suspension effectively interrupts the term of his office. As to the claim that the findings of the Ombudsman run contrary to the well-established doctrines of the Supreme Court in the cases of Arias and Juron which seek to exempt local chief executives from any liability, criminal or administrative, for the negligence of the BAC members, this Department respectfully inhibits itself from this matter. Considering that the subject matter is already being heard and tried under an august body, this Department is constrained to provide further inputs and recommendations on the same based on the principle of litis pendencia or pending litigation. Finally, this opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same. As such, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concern.
